About Me

I started out interested in aerospace engineering, but building a website for my family's retail business revealed a knack for software. By 1996 I had taken that business online with catalogs and e-commerce that grew to 10% of annual sales.

After several years of freelance work, a move to Utah led to my first developer role and my first love in programming: .NET, starting with version 1. That became a career of senior, lead, and architect roles at companies including the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Visa, J.P. Morgan Chase, and Quark.

Since 2009 I've run WireServers, a web development firm, and today I'm lead architect at CenterLight Healthcare, building a greenfield EHR platform with a team of five. I work AI-first, using Claude Code, custom skills, and MCP servers for code generation, reviews, and tests.

Education: Metropolitan State University of Denver

Architecture & Technical Leadership

Security & Compliance
